before.title: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis
before.diseaseDescription: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis: autoimmunity, endothelial injury, fibroblast activation and skin fibrosis, with interstitial lung disease and renal crisis branches. Mixed-subset SSc studies retain their context; excludes limited cutaneous disease, morphea and overlap syndromes.
before.releaseNote: Consolidated local dcSSc candidate. Antibody associations, culture mechanisms, inferred vascular niches and renal phenotypes remain distinguished. Null findings are retained; no universal circuit, independent review or calibrated scores asserted.

after.title: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis
after.diseaseDescription: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis: autoimmunity, endothelial injury, fibroblast activation and skin fibrosis, with interstitial lung disease and renal crisis branches. Mixed-subset SSc studies retain their context; excludes limited cutaneous disease, morphea and overlap syndromes.
after.releaseNote: Consolidated dcSSc map with six selected therapies. US SSc-ILD approvals are distinguished from guideline-supported uses without verified SSc-specific approval. Tocilizumab trial corrections remain partly unresolved; negative endpoints and selected-population limits retained. Scientific review pending.

after.label: Severe dcSSc global outcome
after.description: SCOT hierarchical composite of death, organ-failure-free survival, FVC, disability and skin score; not equivalent to isolated skin efficacy.

after.text: Captopril controlled blood pressure in a four-patient SRC case series.
limitations: Small uncontrolled series; inhibition of the renin–angiotensin pathway is mapped, ACE itself is not a separate node.

after.text: The historical SRC cohort had higher one-year survival in the ACE-inhibitor era (76% versus 15%).
limitations: Nonrandomized historical comparison; secular confounding; use at established SRC is distinct from prophylaxis.

after.text: In SLS II, cyclophosphamide recipients had improved FVC percent predicted from baseline to 24 months (+2.88 points).
limitations: Within-arm improvement; toxicity and withdrawal differed; no assertion of equal efficacy.

after.text: Cyclophosphamide caused more leukopenia and premature treatment withdrawal than MMF in SLS II.
limitations: Harms qualify therapeutic use; this is not an endpoint-specific efficacy contradiction.

after.text: SCOT favoured myeloablative autologous HSCT over monthly cyclophosphamide on the 54-month global rank composite (P=0.01).
limitations: 75 selected severe scleroderma participants; comparator is cyclophosphamide, not all current treatments.

after.text: SCOT transplant treatment-related mortality was 3% at 54 months and 6% at 72 months, versus 0% with cyclophosphamide.
limitations: Treatment selection and cardiopulmonary screening are essential; not generalizable to advanced cardiorespiratory involvement.

after.text: SLS II did not confirm the hypothesised MMF superiority over cyclophosphamide (primary analysis P=0.24).
limitations: 142 randomized, 126 in primary analysis; negative superiority result is not equivalence.

after.text: In SLS II, MMF recipients had improved FVC percent predicted from baseline to 24 months (+2.19 points).
limitations: Within-arm improvement; no placebo arm; does not prove superiority or equivalence to cyclophosphamide.

after.text: SENSCIS primary analysis found slower annual FVC decline with nintedanib (difference 41.0 mL/year, 95% CI 2.9–79.0).
limitations: 576 treated; 51.9% diffuse cutaneous; lung-function slowing is not fibrosis reversal.

after.text: SENSCIS multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses gave P values of 0.06–0.10, qualifying the positive primary result.
limitations: Sensitivity to handling missing data; no mortality benefit asserted.

after.text: SENSCIS did not show a significant skin-score benefit (difference -0.21, 95% CI -0.94 to 0.53).
limitations: Secondary outcome, no human skin efficacy inferred from preclinical antifibrotic activity.

after.text: Nintedanib inhibited proliferation and migration of SSc-ILD lung fibroblasts in culture.
limitations: Fibroblasts are an indirect cellular target; direct targets are kinases, not PDGF ligand.

after.text: focuSSced secondary FVC findings favoured tocilizumab (4.2 percentage-point difference, nominal analysis).
limitations: Primary skin endpoint failed; selected early inflammatory dcSSc; two linked correction notices could not be fully inspected. Current US label independently confirms SSc-ILD indication.

after.text: Tocilizumab inhibits IL-6 signalling by binding IL-6 receptors.
limitations: IL-6 is an indirect mapped target; receptor is not separately represented.

after.text: focuSSced did not meet the primary skin fibrosis endpoint (adjusted difference -1.73, 95% CI -3.78 to 0.32; P=0.10).
limitations: No demonstrated primary skin benefit; original trial correction details remain pending.

after.name: ACE inhibitors (captopril representative)
after.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme and reduces angiotensin signalling; RAAS is an indirect pathway target.
after.indication: EULAR: use immediately at diagnosis of SRC. This record does not endorse prophylactic use.
after.jurisdiction: United States approvals where explicitly verified; EULAR guidance separately labelled
after.trialPhase: Completed clinical study; population and endpoints restricted as described
limitations: Guideline-supported use. The schema has no off-label category: unverified denotes no SSc-specific regulatory approval verified here, not experimental clinical practice.
Renal recovery is variable; survival evidence is primarily historical observational.

after.name: Cyclophosphamide
after.mechanismOfAction: Broad immunosuppression; clinical lung-function effects are indirect, not direct target binding.
after.indication: Guideline-supported SSc-ILD; toxicity constrains treatment. No SSc-specific approval asserted.
after.jurisdiction: United States approvals where explicitly verified; EULAR guidance separately labelled
after.trialPhase: Completed clinical study; population and endpoints restricted as described
limitations: Guideline-supported use. The schema has no off-label category: unverified denotes no SSc-specific regulatory approval verified here, not experimental clinical practice.
Not a preferred treatment recommendation or universal disease reversal claim.

after.name: Autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation
after.modality: Myeloablative immunosuppression and autologous stem-cell rescue
after.mechanismOfAction: High-intensity immunosuppression followed by stem-cell rescue; global disease outcome is an indirect clinical effect, not a molecular target.
after.indication: EULAR: selected early severe dcSSc with poor prognosis, without advanced cardiorespiratory involvement.
after.jurisdiction: United States approvals where explicitly verified; EULAR guidance separately labelled
after.trialPhase: Completed clinical study; population and endpoints restricted as described
limitations: Procedure status is not equivalent to a drug indication; no regulatory approval claimed.
Treatment-related mortality and strict specialist selection apply.

after.name: Mycophenolate mofetil
after.mechanismOfAction: Immunosuppressive treatment; the mapped clinical lung-function outcome is an indirect effect, not a direct molecular target.
after.indication: Guideline-supported SSc-ILD use; trial duration and tolerability apply. No SSc-specific approval asserted.
after.jurisdiction: United States approvals where explicitly verified; EULAR guidance separately labelled
after.trialPhase: Completed clinical study; population and endpoints restricted as described
limitations: Guideline-supported use. The schema has no off-label category: unverified denotes no SSc-specific regulatory approval verified here, not experimental clinical practice.
Direct IMPDH target and immune-cell mechanisms are not separately curated.

after.name: Nintedanib
after.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits receptor tyrosine kinases including PDGFR, FGFR and VEGFR; mapped fibroblast effects are indirect.
after.indication: US: slowing pulmonary-function decline in adults with SSc-ILD. No skin indication asserted.
after.jurisdiction: United States approvals where explicitly verified; EULAR guidance separately labelled
after.trialPhase: Completed clinical study; population and endpoints restricted as described
limitations: Diarrhoea was frequent; not a fibrosis cure or proven skin treatment.

after.name: Tocilizumab
after.mechanismOfAction: IL-6 receptor blockade inhibits downstream IL-6 signalling; IL-6 ligand is an indirect target.
after.indication: US: slowing pulmonary-function decline in adults with SSc-ILD; subcutaneous use. No general dcSSc skin approval asserted.
after.jurisdiction: United States approvals where explicitly verified; EULAR guidance separately labelled
after.trialPhase: Completed clinical study; population and endpoints restricted as described
limitations: Trial secondary lung result; primary skin endpoint negative; original correction notices remain incompletely resolved.
